outcome_verbatim: "Within-participant comparisons of baseline vs follow-up P values showed that patients had ... a modest increase in working status (170 [28.9%] vs 208 [35.4%]; P < .001) ... (eTable 2 in Supplement 1)". The report never defines what 'working status' counted: no definition, instrument or window is given anywhere in the article, and eTable 2 is not held.
source_locator: Results, Study Population, p. 553 (reporting eTable 2 in Supplement 1, not held)
conflict_note: UNRESOLVED. The report states twice that 618 participated ("Of 921 individuals recruited at baseline, 618 participated in the present study"; "Of 618 participants, 427 (69.1%) were male") and then reports 208 (35.4%) in working status at follow-up. 208/618 = 33.7%, not 35.4%, so the count and the percentage cannot both be right against the only denominator the report states. CANDIDATE RESOLUTION, recorded as a candidate and NOT applied (prompt rule 14, D12.3d): the McNemar within-participant comparison uses only pairs with both baseline and follow-up status, and 170/588 = 28.91% and 208/588 = 35.37% both round to the printed values, so the base is probably 588. That is a reconstruction by this extractor, not an authority, so the status stays `unresolved` and the numerator is not paired with a denominator. Other variables in the same sentence imply yet other bases (76 and 62 supported housing and 52 and 8 legal problems imply 612; 432 and 441 second-generation antipsychotic imply 618), which is consistent with item-level missingness but is never stated. An author reply giving the denominator for working status would resolve this.
notes: DENOMINATOR UNRECOVERABLE: n_outcome_observed is left blank because recovering it needs back-calculation from a printed percentage, which the codebook forbids. reported_percentage_base is also left blank because the base is not printed, only implied. n_assessed = 618 (participated in the follow-up study); n_entered = 921 (recruited at baseline). n_female = 191 is 618 - 427 male, both printed integers, so no percentage was back-calculated. n_employed_baseline = 170 is the baseline arm of the same within-participant comparison and carries the same unstated denominator. ascertainment coded point_prevalence because the reassessment was a single visit at which all baseline measures were repeated, but the report never states an ascertainment window; see unresolved_queries.md.

notes: THE ONLY PAID-WORK COUNT IN THIS REPORT. 4/21 = 19.0% as printed. NOT eligible for the primary pool: ascertainment is attainment at any time during the 12-month follow-up sustained for at least 3 months, not point prevalence, and the cohort is employment-selected. notes: FOLLOW-UP IS NOT AN ELAPSED TIME. Outcomes are attainment "during their engagement in the IPS program", which ran March 2006 to February 2013 and closed for everyone at once when the Commonwealth DES funding changed; individual engagement periods are never reported. Elapsed follow-up therefore varies from days to 84 months with a shared calendar end, which is followup_basis = calendar_end_common under D12.8 and is barred from every landmark horizon. followup_months is left blank rather than filled with the 84-month programme span, which is not any participant's follow-up. NOT paid_any, despite the label "employment outcome". Table 4 shows that the 92 placements behind this count include Volunteer Work (3) and an Unpaid Work Experience Position (1), so some participants counted here attained only unpaid activity, and the report does not say how many. 63 = 31 competitive + 8 non-competitive + 24 type not specified.
